title: React Deployment Core Check
description: Check your understanding of production builds, Git workflows, Docker, Netlify, Vercel, CI/CD, environment configuration, and caching.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does `npm run build` commonly produce for a React SPA?

options.text: Static optimized assets ready to serve

questions.explanation: A production build usually outputs static HTML, JS, CSS, and assets.

questions.prompt: Why should lockfiles be included in deployment workflows?

options.text: They help CI and teammates install reproducible dependencies

questions.explanation: Lockfiles make dependency installation more predictable across machines and CI.

questions.prompt: What is the common Docker production pattern for a React SPA?

options.text: Build static assets, then serve them from a lightweight web server such as Nginx
Run the Vite dev server in production
Expose source files directly with no build

questions.explanation: The Docker lesson describes building static assets and serving them from a production web server.

questions.prompt: What do Netlify SPA redirects usually solve?

options.text: Direct visits to client-side routes returning 404

questions.explanation: SPAs need fallback routing so paths handled by the client route to the app entry point.

questions.prompt: What is a Vercel preview deployment useful for?

options.text: Reviewing a branch before promoting or merging
Storing private tokens in the browser

questions.explanation: Preview environments let teams inspect branch changes before production release.

questions.prompt: What should a CI pipeline commonly check before deployment? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Manually edit production files over SSH

questions.explanation: CI should automate repeatable quality checks such as install, lint, test, and build.

questions.prompt: Which cache strategy is appropriate for hashed JS and CSS build assets?
questions.explanation: Hashed filenames support long caching because a content change produces a new URL.

questions.prompt: Frontend build-time environment variables are safe places for private secrets because users cannot inspect production bundles.
questions.explanation: Client bundles are inspectable, so build-time frontend values must be treated as public.
